chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Leaves in New York and Condon's plan for a club
summary: On leaves he plays Town Hall with Condon, who says he is opening a club; soldiers crowd round Davison's car radio to hear Condon's broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah --but you did have a pretty good time musically--
Oh, musically yes. There were some great musicians---
And, when you had a leave, you usually went back to New York and ended up making records and stuff.

Well, on a leave--- everytime I had a leave, I wound up doing Town Hall with Condon and all this stuff - and this is when we cooked up the (inaudible). He said, now you know, I'm opening a joint - you know, I'm opening up Eddie Condon's Club and I want you in the thing and the minute you get out of th Army, I want you to let me know because we're going to be opening.
You were actually in the Army just about two years - weren't you?
About two years and four months - I think it was.
Oh, you actually got out in early '46 then.
Well, as soon as they touched the bomb off

Well, I certainly envied all the guys that were making all the money. Condon was really making it and he had his T.V. shows and his Town Hall Concerts and, uh, I used to --- the guys in the band - I had a car in the Army with a radio and he used to do those blue network shows on Saturdays and I'd have 200 of the band musicians around my car listening to the radio-- when Condon was on the blue network.
